name: GLP-1 for facial leaning

card.summary: Using GLP-1 weight-loss medications to lose body fat, including in the face, for a leaner, more defined jawline and cheekbones.
card.note: Prescription drugs with gastrointestinal side effects; weight loss can also bring lean-mass loss and a gaunt face.

quick.overview:
GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Zepbound) are prescription medications that reduce appetite and body weight. Some people in appearance-focused communities consider them as a route to lose facial fat and reveal jaw and cheek definition.

In trials of semaglutide, adults with obesity lost about 14.9 percent of body weight over 68 weeks versus about 2.4 percent on placebo.[1] Fat loss in the face follows overall weight loss rather than being targeted, and a gaunt look sometimes called Ozempic face is a recognized concern in discussion of rapid loss.
quick.how: These drugs are prescribed as injections (and in some cases tablets) under medical supervision for diabetes or obesity. Users on fitness forums describe pairing them with strength training and high protein intake to keep muscle while losing fat. No dosing details are given here.
quick.risks: Common effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation and abdominal pain, mostly during dose escalation. Labels carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors based on rodent data, and gallstones are reported. Lean mass can fall, and regain after stopping is common.[1] Rapid facial fat loss can read as hollow or aged.

lead: GLP-1 for facial leaning refers to the use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, mainly semaglutide and tirzepatide, to lower body fat with the aim of a slimmer, more sculpted face. For some people, reducing facial fullness sharpens the jawline and cheekbones, which is the appearance goal behind the practice.

The drugs were approved for type 2 diabetes first, with Ozempic approved in the US in December 2017 and Wegovy for weight management in June 2021.[1] Fat loss from these drugs is systemic and cannot be directed at the face. A 2024 review cited on semaglutide found lean body mass decreased in some studies while the lean-to-total mass ratio rose in all of them.[1]

Members of strength-training forums such as T Nation discuss GLP-1 drugs for fat loss, including articles asking whether they work and whether they are safe, and logs by users who lost large amounts of weight and then had to regain lean mass.[2][3]

chain: GLP-1 drug lowers appetite and body weight
Overall body fat, including facial fat, falls
Sharper jaw and cheek definition (or a gaunt look if loss is extreme)
angle.text: The drug works through appetite and weight; face slimming is a side result of general fat loss. People pursuing a leaner face use it alongside resistance training to preserve muscle.

paras: Online, people describe using GLP-1 drugs to lose body fat so the face looks leaner. One T Nation forum user reported dropping from 207 to 127 pounds on Zepbound over a year and then being asked by their doctor to regain lean mass.[3] Another thread covers a user's 25-pound loss over ten weeks.[4]
Semaglutide is indicated for type 2 diabetes, weight management, cardiovascular risk reduction and certain liver disease in the US, with brands including Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy.[1]

In a 2021 phase III trial of 1,961 adults with obesity, semaglutide produced about 14.9 percent weight loss at week 68 versus 2.4 percent for placebo. A 2025 systematic review found people regain about 67 percent of lost weight within a year of stopping.[1]

Gastrointestinal effects are dose-dependent and usually peak during the first 8 to 12 weeks. Other reported risks include gallstones, a boxed thyroid C-cell tumor warning based on rodent studies, and temporary worsening of diabetic retinopathy with rapid glucose lowering. Heart rate rises by about 3 beats per minute on average.[1]
Loss of lean mass is reported in some studies, which is why forum users and clinicians discuss resistance training and protein intake alongside the drugs.[1][3]
T Nation published an article on semaglutide that mentions Elon Musk and Kim Kardashian as reported users, framing the question of whether the drugs work and are safe.[2]
Trials of semaglutide measure total body weight, not facial fat. No published trial has tested GLP-1 drugs specifically for facial leaning.

timeline.event: Ozempic approved in the US for type 2 diabetes.[1]
Wegovy approved in the US for weight management; phase III trial reports 14.9% loss at 68 weeks.[1]
